Bill.BriefDescription: Imposing a minimum bail bond premium fee of ten percent.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to the imposition of a minimum bail bond premiumfee of ten percent; adding new sections to chapter 18.185 RCW; creatinga new section; and prescribing penalties.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature recognizes that corporatesurety bail bond premium fees that fall below ten percent of thepenalty amount of the bond to be posted encourage flight and thus makeit more likely that a defendant will forfeit the bond and fail toappear in court at the designated time. Accordingly, the legislatureintends to create uniformity of law and promote public safety bycreating a standard bail bond premium fee throughout the state.

(1) A bail bond agent shall charge andcollect for his or her premium, commission, or fee an amount of tenpercent of the amount of the corporate surety bail bond posted by himor her. (2) The bail bond agent shall certify to the court that thepremium, commission, or fee is at least ten percent of the amount of p. 1 SB 6312the corporate surety bail bond posted by him or her. The certificationshall be submitted to the court along with the bond. (3) Subsection (1) of this section applies to a bond posted forpersons convicted of a crime against a person, as provided in RCW9.94A.411.

(1) The director may impose a civil penaltyfor a violation of this chapter. The civil penalty shall consist of: (a) For a first violation, a written warning and a monetary penaltyof one thousand dollars; (b) For a second violation, mandatory suspension of the bail bondagent's license for a maximum of one year and a monetary penalty of onethousand dollars; (c) For a third violation, mandatory revocation of the bail bondagent's license and a monetary penalty of five thousand dollars. (2) At the request of the director, the attorney general may bringan action in the name of the state seeking: (a) Injunctive relief to prevent the bail bond agent from furtherviolation of this chapter; (b) To recover civil penalties imposed under subsection (1) of thissection; or (c) To recover attorneys' fees and other enforcement costs anddisbursements.
All revenues derived from any civilpenalties assessed under section 3 of this act shall be deposited inthe business and professions account, pursuant to RCW 43.24.150(1)(f).
Sections 2 through 4 of this act are eachadded to chapter 18.185 RCW.
